newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ short end sold at close as Kiwi falls away.
newsitem.headline: NZ short end sold at close as Kiwi falls away.

text.p: * NZ short end suffers from weaker currency at close
The short end of New Zealand's yield curve suffered at Monday's close as the currency dropped to US$0.6922/29 from its 0.6963/70 open.

Ninety-day bank bills ended 11 points higher at 9.97 percent as the New Zealand dollar Trade-Weighted Index dropped to 66.16 from its 66.62 open. December futures contracts ended 15 points higher at 90.50.

"I believe there hasn't been an obvious large seller (of the Kiwi). It's just the same as the bonds -- bits and pieces, traders not wanting to hold onto too much. Everything is just getting very thin pre-election," one bond dealer said.
Forex dealers blamed political opinion polls for the bearish sentiment.
New Zealanders go to the polls this Saturday for the country's first general election under a proportional voting system which favours a minority or coalition government.
Recent polls have shown support for the ruling conservative National party falling away and the main opposition Labour party rising dramatically to fill the gap.

If Labour, the left-wing Alliance and the economic nationalist New Zealand First party can stitch together a coalition arrangement, together they would glean enough support to oust National, according to the polls.

The polls met with a subdued reaction from financial markets, which have been alarmed by the economic policies of the Alliance and NZ First in particular. They were sufficient to quash any rally on the back of U.S. strength overnight, and the
market opened only slightly stronger, with domestic institutional sellers waiting in the wings.
By the close, three year bond yields were up seven basis points at 7.95 percent and the 10 year maturities were off one at 7.84 percent.

"It looked like there were a couple of long positions, particularly in the shorter bonds, that carried over from last week...maybe there was a bit of stop-loss selling in those, which has pushed down a couple of spreads," a dealer said.
Ongoing samurai and eurokiwi interest on the back of attractive New Zealand yields was not expected to be dampened at all by election uncertainty.
